channel.title: OnlyBills articles
channel.description: Splitting the bill, tipping and money with friends.

item.title: Can you split a bill with Zelle?
item.description: Zelle has no split button of its own, but some banks add one. How to split with Chase or U.S. Bank, request vs send, and why there's no Zelle link.

item.title: How friends pay each other back in Europe, country by country
item.description: Spain uses Bizum, Sweden Swish, the Netherlands Tikkie. What locals use in each European country, and what works if you're visiting without a local bank.

item.title: How friends pay each other back in Latin America
item.description: What locals share to get paid back in Argentina, Mexico, Colombia, Peru and Chile, how each one works, and what to do if you don't have a local bank.

item.title: How to pay a friend back by IBAN, and how fast it arrives
item.description: Send to their IBAN and the exact name on the account. Euro instant transfers arrive within 10 seconds, and your bank now checks the name before you pay.

item.title: How to split a bill on Cash App
item.description: Cash App has no split button, but requests, payment links and Pools do the job. Friends without Cash App can pay a link with Apple Pay or Google Pay.

item.title: How to split a bill on Venmo
item.description: Split a purchase, scan a receipt or request different amounts on Venmo, add tax and tip fairly, and what to do when a friend isn't on Venmo.

item.title: How to split a bill when everyone uses a different payment app
item.description: Venmo, Cash App, Zelle, PayPal or Apple Cash? Who needs which account, which ones work without one, and one message that lets every friend pay you back.

item.title: How to split a bill with Bizum in Spain
item.description: How Spanish friends split a bill with Bizum, what to do if you don't have a Spanish bank, the limits, and a worked example in euros.

item.title: How to split a bill with Interac e-Transfer
item.description: Work out each share, then use Request Money in your bank app, one request per friend. Some banks split for you. Fees, timing and request scams to avoid.

item.title: How to split a bill with Pix in Brazil
item.description: How friends in Brazil split a bill with Pix, what Pix Copia e Cola is, which Pix key to share, and how to split the 10% service charge fairly.

item.title: How to split a bill with Swish, Vipps or MobilePay
item.description: Swish has Dela kostnad, Vipps has Split an amount, MobilePay has requests. How each splits a bill, how to do uneven shares, and what visitors can use.

item.title: How to split a check with tax and tip
item.description: Split tax and tip in proportion to what each person ordered. The one-line formula, a worked $183.78 example, tip before or after tax, and the last cent.

item.title: How to split groceries with roommates (fairly, by item)
item.description: Three ways to split groceries with roommates, how to handle shared staples vs personal items, a worked $96 receipt, and how to settle up without nagging.

item.title: Splitting a bill abroad: which currency should friends pay you back in?
item.description: Friends should pay you back in your own currency, at a rate you all agree at the table. Worked examples, card fees and which exchange rate is fair.

item.title: The best bill splitting apps in 2026
item.description: Venmo, Cash App, Apple Cash, Zelle, Splitwise, Tricount, Settle Up and OnlyBills compared: who each suits, what's free, and who needs an account.

item.title: Tikkie, Wero and iDEAL explained: paying friends in the Netherlands and nearby
item.description: A Tikkie is a payment request you pay through iDEAL, which is becoming Wero. How each works, where Wero is live, and how to pay without a Dutch bank.

item.title: Tipping and service charge by country, and how to split them
item.description: Do you tip in Spain? What's coperto? Is Brazil's 10% optional? What's on the bill and what's expected, country by country, and how to split it fairly.

item.title: Buying rounds in a UK pub: the etiquette
item.description: How rounds work in a UK pub, the unwritten rules, what to do when someone skips their round or drinks pricier drinks, and when a tab or split is fairer.

item.title: Corkage and cakeage fees: costs and how to split them
item.description: Corkage is a per bottle fee for bringing your own wine, cakeage a per head fee for your own cake. Typical UK costs, and how to split them when only some had it.

item.title: Cover charges in the UK: do you have to pay?
item.description: A cover charge is a fixed fee per diner. When it's legal in the UK, whether you have to pay it, if it goes to staff, and how to split it fairly on a group bill.

item.title: Graduation dinner: who pays, and how to split it
item.description: Who usually pays for a UK graduation meal, whether the graduate should, and how to split it fairly when two families share a table. With £ examples.

item.title: Group booking deposits: who pays and how to split them
item.description: Who pays a restaurant deposit for a group, how it comes off the bill, what happens when someone drops out, and whether no-show fees are legal in the UK.

item.title: How long does a bank transfer take in the UK?
item.description: Faster Payments usually land almost immediately, but can take up to two hours. Why some are held, and the quickest way to pay a friend back after dinner.

item.title: How to avoid an awkward bill split
item.description: Most awkward bill splits are decided before anyone orders. What to say before the meal, at the table and afterwards, with messages you can copy and a £ example.

item.title: How to pay a friend back without their bank details
item.description: Ask for their payment link, send a claim link from your bank, use PayPal or pay cash. What each way needs from you, plus limits, speed and safety checks.

item.title: How to say you only want to pay for what you had
item.description: On a budget, eating light or saving up? Why paying for what you had isn't rude, when to mention it, and word for word lines for the group chat and the table.

item.title: How to send the bill to the group chat
item.description: What to send after a group meal, when to send it, messages you can copy, what a shared bill link looks like in iMessage and how to chase gently if nobody pays.

item.title: How to split a bill when some pay cash and some pay card
item.description: Some friends have cash, some only cards. How to settle one bill so nobody loses out: who takes the cash, the change, card minimums and a worked £ example.

item.title: How to split a bill with a discount or voucher
item.description: Who gets the saving when a group bill has a voucher, 2 for 1 deal or dining card discount, and how to share it fairly, with worked £ examples to the penny.

item.title: How to split a bottomless brunch bill fairly
item.description: How to split a bottomless brunch when some take the drinks package and some don't, plus time limits, service charge and deposits. With a worked £ example.
